title: tickadoo — book a West End night with your agent
pitch: The agent finds the show and lights the dates. You tap Book.
about_excerpt: The agent finds the show and lights the dates. You tap Book. Like Comment Story Updates Why this is a strong fit for WebMCP This is the live tickadoo storefront. A person still taps Book. Buying theatre tickets is a page you already trust, not a hackathon toy. Dates, seats, and price only make sense on the live product page. Remote MCP can search a catalog. It cannot move the calendar you are looking at, or stop an agent from inventing a checkout. WebMCP lets ChatGPT and Chrome call the same search and availability tools on www.tickadoo.com , then write the result back into the page the person can see. How it creates a better user experience You stay on tickadoo. Ask for West End tonight, or for dates on a specific show. The listing updates, or the calendar highlights real available nights. You still press Book. There is no pay tool. Cart, checkout, and account URLs are blocked from agent navigation. The agent does the hunting. The person does the money. What people and agents can do together that was hard before Before: an agent either guessed through the UI or quoted a catalog card in another window, while you tried to match that to the real page. After: the agent and the page share one session. search_events refreshes the visible search or London listing. whats_on_tonight opens /london/today. get_availability highlights dates on the show calendar when that UI is on screen. You confirm. That is a shared buyer path, not a scrape. How we implemented WebMCP www.tickadoo.com already ran on Cloudflare Workers (TanStack Start, apps/www in tickadoo/frontend). During the submission window we registered tools with document.modelContext.registerTool in the existing client bundle (apps/www/src/lib/webmcp.ts, wired from entry-client.tsx). Tools call the live catalog at https://mcp.tickadoo.com/mcp (search_experiences, availability, details). Page language and city come from the URL. A small live-page bridge updates search, /london/today, and calendar highlights without replacing checkout. tickadoo_open_product can open product, search, city, and booking-date URLs only. This is an existing-app extension, not a greenfield demo. Prior WebMCP on www (before 25 Aug 2026) exposed a thin 3-tool proxy. Challenge work is frontend#2935, merged to main as c8a0fa0 on 27 Aug 2026: search_events, get_availability, get_experience_details, whats_on_tonight, locale context, in-page actuation, and a hard block on checkout/cart/account. Judges should score the PR, not the older proxy. Optional Chrome Origin-Trial header is wired (WEBMCP_ORIGIN_TRIAL_TOKEN) and currently empty. Prefer ChatGPTs in-app browser, which supports WebMCP without the token. Chrome 149+ works with chrome://flags/#enable-webmcp-testing. How judges should test Open ChatGPT desktop → in-app browser (preferred). Or Chrome 149+ with chrome://flags/#enable-webmcp-testing. Go to https://www.tickadoo.com/london/the-lion-king-tickets Ask: Find West End shows I can see tonight. You should land on or see /london/today. On that show page, ask: Which dates are available next month? The calendar should highlight real nights. Do not ask it to pay. Click Book yourself. Stop on the human checkout. Confirm tools exist in the page bundle: search_events, get_availability, whats_on_tonight. No login. No API key. Do not complete a paid booking.
